## 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

- **Headline revenue growth is flattered by one-off invoicing.** Monthly recurring revenue (MRR) grew only **+1.6%** from €746.1k in September to €757.7k in October. Invoiced revenue grew **+9.6%** (€797.1k → €873.4k), but that is driven by a €120k annual invoice for Gringotts and €5.7k of professional services, not by underlying recurring growth.
- **Churn is concentrated in SMB starter.** Four of the nine starter-plan customers active in September churned in October: Slate Rock, Mega-lo-Mart, Dinoco, and Buy n Large. That is **44% monthly churn** in that sub-segment and represents **€25.3k of MRR that will hit November**.
- **The Pro plan is the highest-margin plan but is deteriorating.** Pro contribution margin fell from **67.5% to 62.7%** in one month. Support cost per Pro customer rose ~11%, and rate-limit tickets jumped from 5 to 13, mostly from Pro customers.
- **Acquisition data supports a tentative increase in content spend, but CAC payback cannot be calculated** because no channel spend is provided. Partner has the best lead-to-trial conversion but very low volume; paid search has high volume but low conversion and is expansion-dependent.
- **Recommended actions:** reduce investment in SMB starter, tentatively increase content acquisition spend, and point engineering focus at the Pro plan.

---

## 2. REVENUE & CUSTOMER HEALTH

### MRR vs invoiced revenue

| Metric | September | October | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| MRR (plans.csv) | €746,100 | €757,700 | +1.6% |
| Invoiced subscription revenue | €746,100 | €867,700* | +16.3% |
| Invoiced total revenue | €797,100 | €873,400* | +9.6% |

*October subscription total excludes the duplicate Soylent invoice. If the duplicate is counted, October total invoiced revenue is €892.9k (+12.0%).

The gap between MRR and invoiced revenue is explained by Gringotts’ €120k annual invoice in October, which is counted at its €10k monthly equivalent in MRR.

### What is actually driving the numbers

- **New logos added €11.1k MRR in October:** Spacely Sprockets (€3.2k), Cogswell Cogs (€2.1k), Bishop Co (€1.7k), Gekko Co (€2.2k), Paper Street Soap (€1.9k).
- **One expansion added €3.0k MRR:** Hooli’s September-attributed expansion took effect in October (€18k → €21k).
- **One downgrade reduced MRR by €2.5k:** Soylent went from €22k to €19.5k monthly.
- **Churn did not reduce October MRR** because churned customers were invoiced for October before churning. The €25.3k churn will hit November.

### Segment health

- **Enterprise: stable.** No churn. Acme’s request volume fell 45%, but this matches the documented migration from interactive API calls to scheduled batch runs. Revenue was unchanged. This is not a health problem.
- **Mid-market: mixed.** Nakatomi churned in October. Soylent is a concern: usage fell 27%, MRR fell €2.5k, and it generated 8 support tickets in October, including a critical API error ticket.
- **SMB starter: weak.** Four churns, all starter-plan SMBs. New starter logos are very small (€1.7k–€2.2k monthly) and have thin contribution. SMB Pro customers, by contrast, did not churn.

---

## 3. ACQUISITION

### Funnel conversion: leads → paid trial

| Month | Channel | Leads | Trial conversions | Trial conversion rate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Sep | paid_search | 520 | 44 | 8.5% |
| Sep | content | 260 | 31 | 11.9% |
| Sep | partner | 60 | 15 | 25.0% |
| Sep | outbound | 160 | 10 | 6.3% |
| Oct | paid_search | 900 | 58 | 6.4% |
| Oct | content | 330 | 34 | 10.3% |
| Oct | partner | 75 | 17 | 22.7% |
| Oct | outbound | 195 | 11 | 5.6% |

### Attributed revenue by channel

| Channel | New-logo attributed revenue (Sep + Oct) | Expansion attributed revenue (Sep + Oct) | Total attributed revenue |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Partner | €166,800 | €0 | €166,800 |
| Content | €91,200 | €18,000 | €109,200 |
| Paid search | €64,800 | €210,000 | €274,800 |
| Outbound | €56,400 | €24,000 | €80,400 |

### What can and cannot be concluded

- **Can conclude:** Partner has the highest lead-to-trial conversion rate (~23–25%) but very low volume and no new logos in October. Content has consistent trial conversion (~10–12%) and produced new-logo revenue in both months. Paid search has high volume but low trial conversion, and its attributed revenue is heavily weighted toward expansions from existing customers. Outbound has the lowest trial conversion.
- **Cannot conclude:** CAC payback by channel. There is no acquisition spend data in the pack. Without channel cost, we cannot calculate CAC or payback.
- **Cannot conclude:** Trial-to-paid conversion. The funnel tracks leads to paid trial only; the pack explicitly says trial-to-paid conversion is not tracked.
- **Cannot conclude:** True channel ROI. Attributed revenue is annualised contract value at conversion, not cash, and expansion bookings take effect in later billing cycles.

---

## 4. PLAN ECONOMICS

### Contribution after direct costs

| Plan | Month | Customers | Revenue | Infra cost | Support cost | Contribution | Margin | Contribution per customer |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Enterprise | Sep | 14 | €659,000 | €288,000 | €159,000 | €212,000 | 32.2% | €15,143 |
| Enterprise | Oct | 14 | €659,500 | €296,800 | €168,000 | €194,700 | 29.5% | €13,907 |
| Pro | Sep | 8 | €63,000 | €13,600 | €6,900 | €42,500 | 67.5% | €5,313 |
| Pro | Oct | 9 | €66,200 | €16,100 | €8,600 | €41,500 | 62.7% | €4,611 |
| Starter | Sep | 9 | €24,100 | €8,400 | €7,300 | €8,400 | 34.9% | €933 |
| Starter | Oct | 13 | €32,000 | €11,400 | €10,300 | €10,300 | 32.2% | €792 |

### Usage vs included requests

| Plan | Included requests per customer | Avg requests per customer Sep | Avg requests per customer Oct | Avg usage as % of included (Oct) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Enterprise | 3,000,000 | 1,895,714 | 1,888,314 | 63% |
| Pro | 600,000 | 433,125 | 441,889 | 74% |
| Starter | 200,000 | 114,444 | 84,385 | 42% |

On average, no plan exceeds its included request volume. But individual customers do:

- **Enterprise:** Stark (4.29M requests) and Wayne (3.41M) exceed the 3M included level in October.
- **Pro:** Wonka (1.02M), Aperture (705k), and Vandelay (690k) exceed the 600k included level in October.
- **Starter:** No customer exceeds 200k included requests.

### Strongest / weakest plans

- **Strongest by margin:** Pro. Even after the decline, it has a 62.7% contribution margin, far above Enterprise (29.5%) and Starter (32.2%).
- **Largest absolute contributor:** Enterprise. It contributes €194.7k of contribution in October, but its margin fell 2.7 points in one month and its cost per customer rose.
- **Weakest:** Starter. It has the lowest contribution per customer (€792 in October), the lowest margin (32.2%), and the highest churn. New starter customers are too small to move the needle.

---

## 5. RECOMMENDATIONS

### 1. Reduce investment in SMB starter — supported

The data supports reducing investment in the **SMB starter sub-segment**, not SMB as a whole. SMB Pro customers are on the highest-margin plan and did not churn. SMB starter customers:

- Churned at 44% monthly (4 of 9 September starter customers).
- Have the lowest contribution per customer (€792 in October).
- Are being replaced by very small new logos (€1.7k–€2.2k monthly).

Reallocate customer success, sales, and marketing effort away from starter-plan SMB acquisition and toward Pro and Enterprise.

### 2. Increase spend on content — tentatively supported

Content is the most defensible channel to increase spend based on this data:

- Consistent trial conversion: 11.9% in September, 10.3% in October.
- New-logo revenue in both months: €45.6k in September and €45.6k in October.
- It is not dependent on expansions from existing customers.

Partner has higher trial conversion but very low volume and no October new logos. Paid search has high volume but low conversion and is expansion-heavy. **Before increasing content spend, obtain channel cost data to confirm CAC payback.** Without spend, we cannot prove efficiency.

### 3. Focus engineering on the Pro plan — supported

The Pro plan deserves the next quarter’s engineering focus because:

- It is the highest-margin plan, but margin fell from 67.5% to 62.7% in one month.
- Support cost per Pro customer rose ~11% (€862 → €956).
- Rate-limit tickets tripled from 5 to 13, concentrated in Pro customers (Wonka, Aperture, Vandelay, Prestige, Oscorp, Pied Piper, Planet Express).
- Pro customers are exceeding included request volumes, which is generating support load and likely overage complexity.

Engineering should focus on rate limiting, capacity, and cost efficiency for Pro. This protects the highest-margin plan and reduces support cost.

---

## 6. UNCERTAINTIES / DATA ISSUES

- **Duplicate invoice:** `INV-2026-10-0209` for Soylent appears twice — once from `stripe` and once from `billing_sync`, both for €19,500. October revenue is overstated if both are counted.
- **Churn timing:** October invoices include customers who churned during October (Nakatomi, Slate Rock, Mega-lo-Mart, Dinoco, Buy n Large). They were invoiced in advance, so their churn will reduce November MRR, not October MRR.
- **Soylent data inconsistency:** September invoice was €22,000, October was €19,500, and current ARR is €234k (€19.5k monthly). This suggests a downgrade or a data issue that should be confirmed.
- **CAC payback cannot be calculated:** No acquisition spend data is provided. Any CAC payback figure would be an unsupported assumption.
- **Trial-to-paid conversion is not tracked:** The funnel only shows leads to paid trial. We cannot calculate true conversion from trial to paid customer.
- **Attributed revenue is not cash:** Acquisition revenue is annualised contract value at conversion, and expansion bookings take effect in later billing cycles. It should not be treated as current revenue.
- **Support tickets are not all resolved:** Some tickets are open or pending, so ticket counts are not a complete measure of resolved workload.
- **Plan cost allocation is not explained:** `support_cost_eur` includes fully loaded customer-success staff, but the allocation method is not provided. Plan-level cost comparisons may be affected by allocation assumptions.
- **Acme usage decline is expected:** The 45% drop in Acme requests matches the documented migration to scheduled batch runs. It should not be read as a customer health issue.
